ByteSize.description: A byte size: an integer magnitude with a required unit suffix `b`, `kb`, `mb`, `gb`, or `tb`; units are binary, so `1kb` is 1024 bytes.

manager.description: Package manager or ecosystem name, as `cargo`, `npm`, or `pypi`.

requirement.description: The version requirement this entry declares. Set this or `version`, never both.

version.description: The exact version this entry pins. Set this or `requirement`, never both.

DependenciesConfiguration.description:
The `[dependencies]` table. It states how the catalog is resolved, which packages
the operator names beside the ones the workspace's manifests and lockfiles state,
and the bounds the package index reads and holds under.

command_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound one toolchain run may take before it is killed, 1s to 1h.

index_size.description:
Bytes every indexed package may hold together, 1mb to 16gb. A package that
would cross it is skipped.

package_files.description:
Files one package's selection may hold, 1 to 100000. A package past it is
skipped.

package_size.description:
Bytes one package's selected source may hold, 64kb to 1gb. A package past it is
skipped.

packages.description:
Packages carried beside the ones the workspace's manifests and lockfiles state.
Each entry names exactly one of `version` and `requirement`.

resolution.description:
How the catalog is resolved: `auto` runs each toolchain, `static` reads the
lockfiles and package caches alone.

DependencyResolution.description:
How the resolvers reach a package graph: through each toolchain, or from the
static inputs alone.

oneOf.description:
Each resolver runs its toolchain and answers from its static inputs when the run
fails.

No toolchain runs. Each resolver answers from its static inputs, and an entry only
a toolchain can name is reported as a degradation.

Duration.description: A duration: an integer magnitude with a required unit suffix `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, or `d`.

EmbeddedEngine.description: One engine this build links in, served in process without a command.

oneOf.description: The ty type checker, serving Python semantics in process.

EmbeddingConfiguration.description:
The `[search.vector.embedding]` table: which embedding model runs, and
the bounds its execution keeps. `kind` selects the arm, and each arm
carries only the keys its execution reads.

A `directory` model downloads nothing, so it carries no download keys. An
`openai_compatible` model sends declaration text while vectors are built
and query text while a search runs; `api_key_env` names the environment
variable holding the credential and never carries the credential itself.

oneOf.description:
Weights come from a Hugging Face repository, cached where every other
Hugging Face client on the machine caches them.

batch_inputs.description:
Inputs one embedding pass hands the encoder at once, 1 to 256.
Attention memory grows with the square of `max_tokens`, so a
raised token window wants a lowered batch.

download_attempts.description:
Attempts one model download makes before vector ranking degrades
to lexical for the life of the server, 1 to 10.

download_timeout.description: Wall-clock budget one model download has, 10s to 1h.

max_tokens.description:
Tokens the encoder reads from one input, 32 to 512. What follows
them is truncated.

model.description:
A repository identifier such as `minishlab/potion-retrieval-32M`,
optionally carrying a revision after `@`. Vectors are stored per
model, so changing the value embeds the workspace again.

The model's own `config.json` decides how it is read. A
`model_type` of `model2vec` is a static model, which embeds a
declaration by averaging one row per token; anything else is read
as a BERT checkpoint, which runs a forward pass per batch and
costs minutes rather than seconds over a whole workspace.

oneOf.description:
Weights are a directory the workspace already holds. Nothing is
downloaded.

batch_inputs.description: Inputs one embedding pass hands the encoder at once, 1 to 256.

max_tokens.description:
Tokens the encoder reads from one input, 32 to 512. What follows
them is truncated.

model.description: A workspace-relative directory holding the model files.

oneOf.description:
Vectors come from a service implementing the `OpenAI` embedding
request and response shape at `/embeddings`.

api_key_env.description:
The environment variable holding the credential. The value names
the variable; it never carries the credential.

attempts.description:
Attempts one embedding request makes, 1 to 10. Retries spend the
same request timeout.

batch_inputs.description: Inputs one embedding request carries, 1 to 2048.

endpoint.description:
The base URL the request path is appended to. It uses `https`;
`http` is accepted only when the host is a loopback address.

max_in_flight.description: Embedding requests running at once, 1 to 32.

model.description: The model the service exposes, such as `text-embedding-3-small`.

request_timeout.description: Wall-clock budget one embedding request has, 1s to 5m.

revision.description:
A deployment identifier the operator states, such as a dated
release. It participates in vector invalidation, so an endpoint
serving new weights under one model name gets a new value here.

ExecutionConfiguration.description:
The `[execution]` table. Exact language entries enable execution; this
table owns the workspace-wide bounds.

max_code.description: Bytes one submitted block may hold, 1b to 32kb.

max_concurrent.description: Evaluations running at once across the whole workspace.

max_output.description: Bytes each captured stream keeps, up to 16kb.

HistoryConfiguration.description:
The `[providers.history]` table. The history provider's cost scales with
how far back it walks, so its depth is the budget worth setting.

enabled.description: Whether the history provider runs at all.

max_revisions.description: Revisions the walk covers from the current head, newest first.

enabled.description: Whether syntax, LSP service, and execution are enabled for matched paths.

exclude.description: Path patterns removed from this language's effective matches.

execution.description: Whether caller-provided code may execute under this exact language.

include.description: Replacement path patterns. Absence keeps shipped patterns; an empty list matches none.

lsp.description: Inline LSP process or name of one shared process.

anyOf.description: Name of one shared top-level `[lsp.<name>]` process.
Process used only by this exact language entry.

LanguageLspConfiguration.description: How one exact language selects an LSP process.

LexicalSearchConfiguration.description: The `[search.lexical]` table: how many units the lexical index holds.

units_max.description:
Most units the lexical index holds: one per indexed file, text chunk,
and declaration, 1000 to 50000000. A workspace past it refuses its
rebuild naming this key.

LogsConfiguration.description:
The `[logs]` table. The server records its own diagnostics in the workspace
database, where `rift://logs` reads them back, and this table bounds how
many records the store keeps, how many one read returns, and which targets
are captured at all. The server reads the table at startup, so a change
applies on the next start.

capture.description:
Which targets are recorded, in the `RUST_LOG` spelling `tracing` takes:
comma-separated `target=level` pairs. A target this filter excludes
never reaches the store, whatever the stderr diagnostics carry.

page_records.description: Records one `rift://logs` read returns at most, 1 to 5000.

retention_records.description: Records the store keeps before the oldest are dropped, 100 to 1000000.

LspConfiguration.description: One external LSP process Rift may start.

command.description:
Executable and literal arguments. Rift starts it directly without a
shell. Exactly one of `command` and `embedded` is present.

embedded.description:
Engine linked into the server, run in process in place of a spawned
command. Exactly one of `command` and `embedded` is present, and an
embedded engine takes no `environment` and no
`initialization_options`.

environment.description:
Environment values added on top of the environment the server
inherited.

initialization_options.description:
Options handed to the process at initialize. Must be a JSON object
when present; the LSP server defines its meaning.

output_limit.description:
Bytes of the process's standard error Rift keeps, 1kb to 8mb. The
full size is still reported.

request_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound on each later LSP request, 1s to 10m.

restart.description:
How often Rift replaces this process on its own, and over what
window; the budget spent, the process's own failure surfaces.

retry.description:
How often Rift sends this process the same request again while its
answer stays unsettled - a refusal the process invites again, or an
answer it gave while still analyzing - and how the waits between
those attempts grow.

settle_delay.description:
Quiet the process's work record holds before a read calls it ready,
10ms to 1m. A language server empties its outstanding work several
times inside one project load, so Rift reports the process ready only
once that record has been empty this long at the last engine output
Rift read. Raise it for a process whose load falls silent for longer
than the default between phases.

startup_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound on the process's initialize handshake, 1s to 10m.

PathPattern.description:
Project-relative glob using *, ?, **, and character classes. Forward-slash separated on
every platform, whatever separator the host OS uses natively.

PortRange.description:
The `server.port_range` table: the inclusive loopback range the server
picks the first free port from.

max.description: The highest port the server may bind, at or above `min`.

min.description: The lowest port the server may bind, 1024 or above.

ProvidersConfiguration.description:
The `[providers]` table: the built-in providers run without
configuration, and this table bounds or disables them.

RankingConfiguration.description:
The `[search.ranking]` table: what each ranking input contributes to a
fused score, and how sharply a top rank counts.

The three weights need not sum to 1. The executor normalizes the weights
of the inputs that answered, so an unavailable vector ranking does not
rescale what identifier matching and the lexical ranking returned.

fusion_k.description:
The reciprocal-rank fusion constant, 1 to 1000. A result scores as the
weighted sum of `1 / (k + rank)` over the rankings that returned it, so
a larger value flattens the contribution curve and lets agreement
between the rankings outweigh one ranking's top position.

identifier_weight.description:
The identifier ranking's share of a fused score, 0.0 to 1.0.
Identifier matching ranks a query against indexed declaration and
qualified names.

lexical_weight.description:
The lexical ranking's share of a fused score, 0.0 to 1.0. The lexical
ranking is the `SQLite` full-text index over names, signatures,
attached documentation, declaration source, and selected text files.

vector_weight.description:
The vector ranking's share of a fused score, 0.0 to 1.0. The vector
ranking answers a query that shares no word with the code it should
reach.

RestartPolicy.description:
How often Rift may replace one language engine on its own, and over
what window.

A restart is any start after the first: the first is the start, and
every start that follows it replaces an engine that ended, failed to
start, or stopped answering. A restart older than `window` no longer
counts, so a workspace whose engine dies once a day keeps its full
budget while a crash-looping one spends it and stops.

attempts.description: Restarts allowed inside one window, 0 to 16. Zero never restarts.

window.description: Span the restarts are counted over, 1s to 1d.

RetryPolicy.description:
How often one unsettled operation is attempted again, and how the
waits between attempts grow.

Attempts are numbered from one and the first is counted, so
`attempts = 1` never resends. Each wait is twice the one before it,
held at `delay_limit`; a `delay_limit` below `delay` therefore holds
every wait at `delay_limit`.

The waits carry no jitter. Jitter spreads a set of independent retriers
apart so they stop arriving together; requests to one language engine
serialize on that engine's own slot, so there is never such a set, and
the sequence stays a function of the attempt number alone.

attempts.description: Attempts one operation takes, the first counted, 1 to 64.

delay.description:
Wait before the second attempt, 1ms to 1m. Every later wait
doubles the one before it.

delay_limit.description: Longest wait between two attempts, 1ms to 10m.

SearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search]` table. `ranking` weighs the ranking inputs against each
other, `lexical` and `vector` bound the two indexed rankings, `text`
bounds the lexical chunks derived from visible text files, and
`pool_slots` and `busy_timeout` bound the shared `SQLite` connections
behind search and logs.

busy_timeout.description:
Wall-clock budget one connection waits for a database lock held by
another process before `SQLITE_BUSY`, 100ms to 30s.

lexical.description: How many units the lexical index holds.

pool_slots.description:
Pooled `SQLite` connections the workspace database may open at once,
1 to 16. Search reads and stored logs share this pool.

ranking.description: What each ranking input contributes to a fused score.

text.description: Chunking policy for visible text files in lexical search.

vector.description:
The embedding model that adds vector ranking, and the bounds its
preparation runs under.

allOf.description: server.port and server.port_range are mutually exclusive

ServerConfiguration.description:
The `[server]` table. Filesystem scans and parses run on a bounded
worker pool; this table sets the worker count, bounds the queue wait,
sets how long the server serves with no request before it stops, and
selects the loopback port. The server reads the table at startup, so a
change applies on the next start.

idle_timeout.description:
Wall-clock span after the last served request completes that stops
the server while no request remains active, 1s to 1d.

num_workers.description: Workers running blocking filesystem and parser operations at once, 1 to 64.

port.description:
The exact loopback port the server binds, 1024 or above. Excludes
`port_range`; omitted, the server picks from `port_range` or the
default serving range.

port_range.description:
The loopback range the server picks its port from. Excludes `port`;
omitted, the default serving range applies.

readiness_timeout.description:
Wall-clock bound one request waits for the workspace's index and
its language services to prove they are ready to answer, 1s to 1h.
One deadline: index validation starts it, and once a request
resolves the languages it needs, waiting on those services spends
what remains of it.

worker_queue_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound one request waits for a free worker, 1ms to 1h.

SourceConfiguration.description:
The `[source]` table: which files below the workspace root the index and reads consider
visible, and how many files and bytes the index holds together. `.git`, `.rift`, and
`target` stay invisible whatever this table says.

exclude.description:
Exact file paths or globs dropped from visibility, in [`PathPattern`] syntax. A match
here is dropped even when `include` also matches it.

files.description:
Most files the index holds, 1000 to 5000000. A workspace past it refuses its rebuild
naming this key.

force_include.description:
Exact file paths or globs that stay visible although the workspace's `.gitignore`
hides them, in [`PathPattern`] syntax. A match here needs no `include` match, and a
match `exclude` also names is still dropped.

include.description:
Exact file paths or globs a file must match to stay visible, in [`PathPattern`] syntax.
Empty includes every file `exclude` and `.gitignore` leave standing.

respect_gitignore.description:
Whether the workspace's own `.gitignore` files, root and nested, hide the paths they
match. Global and parent-directory gitignore sources are never read.

workspace_size.description:
Most source bytes the index holds together, 16mb to 64gb. A workspace past it
refuses its rebuild naming this key.

TextSearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search.text]` table. `include` selects which visible paths join the
text index once every language entry has had its claim, and `max_chunk`
bounds the lexical units derived from them.

include.description:
Project-relative path patterns included as plain text when no language claims them.
The default `["**"]` selects every unclaimed visible path; an empty list selects none.

max_chunk.description:
Bytes one lexical chunk may hold, 1kb to 16mb. Larger files are indexed as
several chunks of at most this size.

VectorSearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search.vector]` table: the vector ranking that reaches code sharing
no word with a query, and the bounds its preparation runs under.

Preparation runs behind the answers. A search issued before the vectors
are in is answered lexically and carries a warning naming what is still
missing.

candidates.description:
Declarations the vector ranking returns before the rankings are
fused, 1 to 1000.

candidates_per_file.description:
Declarations one file may contribute to the vector ranking before
the rest of its declarations are dropped, 1 to 64. Without the bound
one file whose declarations all rank well fills `candidates` on its
own, and no other file reaches the candidate list however well it
would have ranked.

disabled.description:
Whether vector ranking is off. Set it when the workspace must not
fetch model weights: search then answers lexically alone and raises no
preparation warning.

embedding.description:
Which embedding model builds the vectors, and the bounds its
execution keeps.

max_vectors.description:
Vectors the workspace may hold, 1000 to 1000000. Embedding stops at the
bound and the search warning says so; each vector costs the model's
dimension in single-precision floats.

description:
The whole `rift.toml`. Every table is optional and defaults to the
behavior documented on it; any key outside these definitions refuses the
file as `configuration_invalid`.

dependencies.description:
Whether the dependency index runs, how the catalog is resolved, which
cataloged packages it indexes, and the bounds it indexes under.

execution.description: Enablement and limits for caller-provided code.

languages.description: Exact language entries keyed by their `name` or `name:dialect` identity segment.

logs.description:
The server's own log records: how many the workspace database keeps,
how many one read returns, and which targets are captured.

lsp.description: Shared LSP processes keyed by name. Language entries select them explicitly.

providers.description: Bounds and switches for the built-in providers.

search.description: Search ranking, visible text chunking, and storage bounds.

server.description: The server's own blocking-work bounds: worker count and queue wait.

source.description:
Which files below the workspace root the index and reads consider visible, and how
many files and bytes the index holds together.
